newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to ask help for the capture of legislator.
newsitem.headline: Manila to ask help for the capture of legislator.

text.p: The Philippines will ask for the help of neighbouring countries, including Malaysia, to capture a legislator charged with statutory rape of an 11-year-old girl, government officials said on Saturday.

Interior and Local Government Secretary Robert Barbers said his department was checking newspapers reports that congressman Romeo Jalosjos fled to the Malaysian state of Sabah after the Supreme Court rejected his plea to quash the rape charges and retract an order for his arrest on December 27.
"We can negotiate through our foreign affairs on his (Jalosjos') whereabouts...If we have an extradition treaty (in those countries) we have no problem," Barbers said.
Justice Secretary Teofisto Guingona told reporters his department would exhaust all legal measures for the immediate capture of Jalosjos.
Guingona said the state would seek the death penalty against Jalosjos, a member of the House of Representatives from President Fidel Ramos's ruling coalition.
Jalosjos, in a petition filed with the court, called the charges a "fairy tale", and accused prosecutors of bowing to media pressure "to satisfy one's appetite for blood".
Government prosecutors have filed two statutory rape charges and 12 counts of lasciviousness against Jalosjos.
Judge Roberto Diokno of the Makati Regional Trail Court recommended that bail not be given on the rape charges and stipulated bail of 40,000 pesos ($1,526) for each charge of lasciviousness.
Manila newspapers reported the case in August at a time of public uproar over crimes involving politicians and other prominent people thought to be beyond the reach of the law.

Prosecutors said in documents filed with the Makati regional trial court that the acts were committed in Jalosjos' apartment. They said he paid the girl amounts ranging up to 10,000 pesos ($385) each time she visited him, and promised to make her a movie star.
The girl's father brought her to the politician in exchange for the money, they said. The father faces a separate charge of exploitation.
